title: Transformers & LLM Internals
blurb: How a modern large language model is built, from self-attention up to model anatomy. The architecture that won, and what's actually inside the boxes labeled 'LLM' in every system diagram.

nodes.label: Self-attention
nodes.description: Query / key / value, scaled dot-product, the softmax, what attention 'looks at'. The single most-important operation in modern AI.
nodes.doneWhen: You can derive scaled dot-product attention from first principles and explain the role of each Q/K/V.

resources.title: The Illustrated Transformer
resources.author: Jay Alammar
resources.annotation: The single best visual intro to self-attention. Eight years old and still uncontested.

resources.title: Attention Is All You Need
resources.author: Vaswani et al.
resources.annotation: The original transformer paper. Required reading; the architecture and the math are both in eight pages.

resources.title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
resources.annotation: Build a GPT from scratch on video in two hours, attention included. After this, the architecture stops feeling like magic.

nodes.label: Multi-head attention
nodes.description: Why multiple heads, what they specialize on, how heads are concatenated and projected. The 'multi-head' that makes the architecture flexible.
nodes.doneWhen: You can implement multi-head attention from scratch in PyTorch.

resources.title: The Annotated Transformer
resources.author: Sasha Rush et al.
resources.annotation: Harvard's line-by-line implementation of 'Attention Is All You Need'. The clearest multi-head reading you can do.

resources.title: PyTorch — nn.MultiheadAttention
resources.annotation: The reference for the production primitive. Read it once after you've implemented MHA yourself; the API choices make more sense afterwards.

nodes.label: The Transformer architecture
nodes.description: Encoder / decoder / decoder-only. The block: attention + feed-forward + residual + norm. How modern LLMs are stacks of identical blocks.
nodes.doneWhen: You can sketch a decoder-only transformer's forward pass on a whiteboard and explain the residual stream.

resources.title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
resources.author: Elhage et al. (Anthropic)
resources.annotation: The residual-stream framing. Once you read this you can never un-see the transformer as a writer-reader system on a shared stream.

resources.title: Stanford CS336 — Language Modeling from Scratch (Spring 2025)
resources.annotation: Stanford's hands-on course on building modern LLMs from scratch. The lecture videos are on YouTube; the assignments are the reason to enroll.

resources.title: nanoGPT
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
resources.annotation: The simplest production-style decoder-only transformer in 300 lines of PyTorch. Read it once end-to-end.

nodes.label: Tokenization (BPE, SentencePiece)
nodes.description: Why we tokenize subwords, how BPE works, how vocabularies are chosen, why tokenization shapes everything downstream (cost, multilinguality, edge-case behavior).
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why a string-length and a token-length differ, and predict tokenization weirdness for code or non-English text.

resources.title: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
resources.annotation: Builds a BPE tokenizer from scratch and shows every weird tokenization edge case you'll meet in production.

resources.title: Hugging Face — The tokenizers tutorial
resources.annotation: The library every production-LLM stack uses. The tutorial is the right depth for understanding the practical API.

resources.title: Tiktokenizer
resources.annotation: Live tokenizer-visualizer for GPT, Claude, Llama, and others. Paste text, see tokens; the fastest intuition-builder.

nodes.label: Positional encoding & RoPE
nodes.description: Sinusoidal vs learned vs RoPE vs ALiBi. Why position matters, and why the rotary embedding family won the modern LLM.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe what RoPE does and why it generalizes better to long contexts than absolute positions.

resources.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
resources.author: Su et al.
resources.annotation: The RoPE paper. Eu Wen Su's blog (rotated embeddings) is a nice companion; the paper has the math.

resources.title: Eleuther — Rotary Embeddings: A Relative Revolution
resources.annotation: The clearest explainer of why RoPE is geometrically appealing. Read after the paper and it clicks.

nodes.label: Pretraining objectives
nodes.description: Next-token prediction (causal LM), masked LM, prefix-LM, span corruption. Why next-token won, and what it means for what an LLM can do.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why next-token-prediction trains a surprisingly capable model.

resources.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
resources.author: Brown et al.
resources.annotation: The paper that established next-token prediction as the dominant objective. Skim sections 1–3 for the framing.

resources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
resources.author: Devlin et al.
resources.annotation: The MLM objective in its canonical form. Read for contrast with causal LM.

nodes.label: Scaling laws & compute economics
nodes.description: Kaplan / Chinchilla / DeepMind scaling laws, parameter count vs data vs compute, the empirical curves. The reason the field moves the way it moves.
nodes.doneWhen: You can read a scaling-law plot and explain what it tells you about training budget.

resources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
resources.author: Kaplan et al.
resources.annotation: The original scaling-laws paper. Read for the empirical curves and the framing that drove every follow-up.

resources.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
resources.author: Hoffmann et al. (DeepMind)
resources.annotation: The Chinchilla paper. The revision that established 'tokens scale with params' as the right budget rule.

nodes.label: Anatomy of a 2026 LLM
nodes.description: What's actually inside a modern frontier model: decoder-only stack, GQA, SwiGLU, RoPE, MoE, KV cache, long-context techniques. The picture you should have when someone says 'an LLM'.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe the anatomy of a typical open-weights 2026 LLM and explain each design choice in one sentence.

resources.title: Llama 3 Herd of Models
resources.author: Meta AI
resources.annotation: Detailed model card for a frontier open-weights model. The architecture, training, and infrastructure all in one document.

resources.title: Mixtral of Experts
resources.author: Jiang et al. (Mistral)
resources.annotation: The clearest open MoE paper. The MoE design choice is now mainstream; read this for the modern reference.

resources.title: The Llama 3 Herd Architecture (annotated)
resources.author: Sebastian Raschka
resources.annotation: Raschka's series annotates the Llama / Mistral / Phi / Gemma stacks one design choice at a time. Excellent gloss on the model cards.
